table.name: airlines
table.purpose: Lookup table of the 12 U.S. airlines operating in the dataset, keyed by uid and referenced by the flights table.

Abbreviation.name: airline_short_name
Abbreviation.description: Short/common brand name of the airline (e.g. 'USAir', 'JetBlue'), one per carrier.

Airline.name: airline_name
Airline.description: Full legal/marketing name of the airline (e.g. 'US Airways', 'JetBlue Airways').

Country.name: country
Country.description: Country of the airline; all 12 rows are 'USA'.

uid.name: airline_id
uid.description: Surrogate primary key identifying the airline; referenced by flights.Airline.

table.name: airports
table.purpose: Lookup table of 100 US airports, keyed by IATA airport code, giving each airport's name, city, and country. It is the reference for the origin and destination airports of flights in the flights table, and presumably relates to airlines via the flights table as well. Note: text values carry trailing spaces, suggesting fixed-width source data imported without trimming.

AirportCode.name: AirportCode
AirportCode.description: Primary key. Three-letter IATA airport code (e.g. APN = Alpena, ABQ = Albuquerque), uniquely identifying each airport. Referenced by flights.SourceAirport and flights.DestAirport.

AirportName.name: AirportName
AirportName.description: Name of the airport (e.g. 'Alpena County Regional'). Not unique: 12 rows share the generic name 'Municipal', and some values appear truncated (e.g. 'Spb', 'AAF' suffixes), suggesting the source data was cut off at a fixed length.

City.name: City
City.description: City where the airport is located (e.g. 'Alpena', 'Anchorage'). Duplicated where several airports serve the same city.

Country.name: Country
Country.description: Full country name; constant 'United States' across all 100 rows, so this dataset covers only US airports.

CountryAbbrev.name: CountryAbbrev
CountryAbbrev.description: Two-letter ISO country code, 'US' for all rows. One row has a trailing space ('US '), indicating inconsistent whitespace in the data.

table.name: flights
table.purpose: One row per flight: a flight number operated by an airline from a source airport to a destination airport. Joins to airlines (carrier) and airports (origin/destination). No single-column primary key is evident; (Airline, FlightNo) is a plausible composite key but is not confirmed by the data shown.

Airline.name: Airline
Airline.description: Foreign key to airlines.uid identifying the carrier operating the flight (e.g. 2=USAir, 4=Southwest, 8=JetBlue, 11=Allegiant, 12=Virgin). 12 airlines, ~100 flights each.

DestAirport.name: DestAirport
DestAirport.description: Foreign key to airports.AirportCode; the destination airport of the flight. Values are 3-letter IATA/FAA codes with a leading space (e.g. 'APN' = Alpena County Regional).

FlightNo.name: FlightNo
FlightNo.description: Flight number identifying the specific flight service; not unique in this table (836 distinct values over 1200 rows), so it identifies a scheduled flight rather than a row instance.

SourceAirport.name: SourceAirport
SourceAirport.description: Foreign key to airports.AirportCode; the origin airport of the flight. Same 3-letter code format with leading space as DestAirport.
